Builder guards (lines 112-119) look sound. The holder must be an l or p. The marker must be the holder's last child with no non-whitespace tail. It is reinserted right after its holder, so it can never jump past unrelated content. printed_text is compared before and after for every unit. lxml moves an element's tail with it, but any such tail is whitespace only and covered by the printed_text check. Only unattributed stanza milestones are moved. No corresp/canonical URN is created or changed, and markers carrying corresp are untouched.

Possible unintended effect, low risk: terminators now sit at lg/div level while start markers sit inside l/p. Any downstream tool that assumes start and end milestones share a parent could behave differently. The real compiler handles this according to the 13 checks.
